visual_observations.observation: Reverse-landscape picker has system navigation on the left. Standard table selected; tested 2D option and Done visible. Internal scrolling clips the explanatory text and 3D row. No private faces visible.
Full dark Your cards stay private cover replaces the picker, with no native scene visible.
Brief blank dark app surface with system bars; no private content.
Opening table toolbar and opaque stage privacy cover in reverse landscape; both toolbar controls fully visible.
Native status and stage both show Your cards stay private; scene remains concealed.
Table ready; Exit, Your turn · Crown table · Orbit claimed 2, and 5 cards, covered visible. No private faces. Lower reveal control clipped below native scroll viewport; toolbar fully visible.
Standard table button pressed/highlighted; the same covered scene remains visible, with no private faces.

First captured closing state: enlarged portrait-layout Closing table toolbar occupies the left portion of the original landscape recording canvas; stage/background is dark and no private face is visible.
Portrait closing toolbar with disabled controls and opaque Your cards stay private stage; original fixed canvas has black sidebars. No private face or Leave dialog.
Full portrait privacy cover remains after toolbar disappears. Status bar appears from frame 60. No private face.

First returned Compose frame is 63. Crown table, Round 1, Orbit claims 2 Crowns, 5 cards and the complete Show hand control appear with the For your eyes only card-back decoration. All returned frames remain concealed; no selection or Leave dialog.

findings.layout: The native toolbar and returned Compose Show hand control are visible. Large native 2D content overflows its scroll viewport: the lower reveal control is only partly visible; this recording does not demonstrate scrolling to or activating it. The picker is also scrolled/clipped internally while its tested 2D option and Done action remain visible.

limits: Every encoded source frame is covered directly or by an independently verified exact-byte match; capture cadence still limits claims about between-frame device states.
No native private card face is visible before the rotation either; this does not establish concealment of a previously revealed native hand.
The fixed 1600 × 720 original canvas projects portrait content into a narrow centered area with black sidebars after rotation. No derivative was resized by this review.
Original packet PTS and source frame order only; no device uptime, host UTC, action, or matching-UP alignment is claimed.
The recording ends before the separate continuity-reveal and portrait re-entry checks; those are not visually qualified here.
